driver_desc: the MIGRATION OF AI VALUE CAPTURE across the software/platform stack — if the frontier-to-open-source model catch-up window stays at ~3-6 months or compresses, raw frontier-model IP commoditizes and durable AI economics migrate to the layers ABOVE the model (application software with workflow/user/data/regulatory moats monetizing AI on proprietary data and installed workflows) and BELOW it (hyperscaler compute, cloud distribution, data gravity). The structure is PARALLEL stack layers, not a supply chain: (1) app-workflow-moat — vertical / system-of-record software with disclosed AI monetization on proprietary data or regulated workflows; (2) hyperscaler-platform — cloud/compute/distribution capturing disclosed inference and AI-deployment economics; (3) model-ip — frontier-model licensing/API economics (the LOSING side if the window holds); (4) open-ecosystem — names whose disclosed economics benefit from open-weights adoption (tooling, serving, customization); (5) silicon-ecosystem-moat — silicon vendors whose MODEL-AGNOSTIC software/developer-ecosystem bundle (programming model, software stack, developer base) captures AI economics whichever model wins — the moat, never the unit volumes. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the MIGRATION (which layer captures AI economics), grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic 'AI' adjacency, NOT the physical AI-datacenter build-out chain (chips/HBM/packaging/cooling/power — build-out economics of ANY shape, unit demand and pricing/mix/contract revenue alike — the ai-datacenter driver; the ONE carve-out routed here is category (5) above), NOT consumer-device AI feature mentions.

the GLP-1 DRUG VALUE CHAIN's SECOND GROWTH PHASE — incretin therapy transitioning from supply-constrained scarcity to a volume-driven, price-competitive, chronic-treatment market: affordability/access expansion, resolution of supply constraints, oral formulations, direct-to-patient distribution, generic/compounded entry, and an induction-to-maintenance chronic model. Treated patient VOLUMES rise while manufacturer PRICING compresses and market share FRAGMENTS — so the equity question is per-name, not category-level. The structure is PARALLEL categories: (1) incumbent-franchise — marketed incretin franchises (two-sided: volume tailwind AND price/share headwind); (2) next-gen-assets — differentiated pipelines (orals, amylin, multi-agonists, muscle-preserving combinations); (3) manufacturing-infra — peptide API, CDMO / fill-finish capacity, devices/auto-injectors (the infrastructure-economics leg); (4) access-distribution — direct-to-patient, pharmacy/telehealth fulfillment, and generic distribution WITH disclosed incretin volume linkage. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the tag says which side a name sits on. Exposure must be to the drug value chain, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT the food/beverage consumption shift (the glp1-demand-shift SIBLING driver), NOT payers/PBMs without disclosed incretin economics, NOT fitness or weight-management services.
